mem.t: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

lessons.title: The Nature of the Battle
lessons.theme: Our real enemy is not people but the powers of darkness

v: For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world’s rulers of the darkness of this age, and against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds,
throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ,

lessons.still: Think of someone who has recently made you angry or hurt you. Softly say before the Lord, “Lord, this person is not my enemy.” Hand your anger toward them over to the Lord, and then turn your eyes to the real battle.
teach: For soldiers fighting in thick fog, the greatest danger is not the enemy but hitting their own side. So it is with many conflicts in families, churches and ministry teams: we take aim at the people next to us and fail to see the real enemy behind them.

Paul says our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, powers and the world rulers of this darkness. Where is the battlefield? 2 Corinthians 10 tells us: “strongholds,” “every high thing,” “every thought.” Satan’s main attack is to build, inside people’s minds, high walls that keep them from knowing God. Our weapons are for “bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ.”

So the first shift in mindset for spiritual warfare is this: people are not my enemies; people need to be won back. The second is this: the battlefield is the mind, not only our circumstances. Ever since Eden, Satan has attacked with the lie, “You will be like God.” Every thought that makes me want to be my own king is a stronghold that must be torn down.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life overcomes Satan. Satan’s very nature is pride; he wants people to leave their place. Our victory is to return to our place and let Jesus reign. We do not fight against people but against pride; we do not rely on the flesh but on the Holy Spirit. Our focus is on Jesus, not on people and not on circumstances.
q: Who is God? — God gives weapons that are “mighty before God.” What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Whom have you recently been treating as an enemy?
How shall I respond? — What “stronghold” in your heart needs to be taken captive and brought into obedience to Christ?
lessons.jesus: When Peter urged Jesus not to take the way of the cross, Jesus said, “Get behind me, Satan!” He did not treat Peter as an enemy, but he discerned the voice behind Peter’s words. He loved Peter, and at the same time rejected the temptation of thinking “not the things of God, but the things of men.”
lessons.pray: Lord, open my eyes to see the real battle. I will no longer treat people as enemies or fight with the weapons of the flesh. Tear down the proud strongholds in my heart, take my thoughts captive, and bring me into complete obedience to Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray a blessing, not an accusation, over someone you are in conflict with
Write down a lie that often attacks you, and find a verse to counter it
Whenever you feel angry today, silently say, “This person is not my enemy.”
lessons.noon: “Throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ” — Lord, right now my thoughts belong to you.

lessons.title: The Whole Armour
lessons.theme: To put on God’s armour is to put on Christ himself

v: Stand therefore, having the utility belt of truth buckled around your waist, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
and having fitted your feet with the preparation of the Good News of peace,
above all, taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one.
And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God;

lessons.still: Stand up and lightly touch, in turn, your waist, your chest, your feet, your arm and your head. With each touch, silently name a piece of armour: truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation. Finally, picture yourself gripping God’s word. Say to the Lord, “I put you on.”
teach: A soldier going into battle does not wear just one piece of armour. Without a helmet, even the best breastplate cannot save his life; with a sword but no boots, he cannot keep his footing. When Paul wrote this letter he was a prisoner for the Lord, and he knew the equipment of Roman soldiers intimately. Through this picture the Holy Spirit teaches us that spiritual protection must be “whole.”

Each piece of armour has its purpose. The belt of truth keeps lies from loosening us; the breastplate of righteousness guards the conscience; the shoes of the gospel of peace give us sure footing, ready at any time to share the good news; the shield of faith quenches the fiery arrows of the evil one; the helmet of salvation guards our thinking; the sword of the Spirit, the word of God, is our weapon of attack. These are not merely techniques. They point to Christ himself: he is the truth, our righteousness, our peace and our salvation.

So putting on the armour really means “putting on the Lord Jesus Christ” every day (Romans 13:14). It is not enough to recite a formula once in the morning. Every time a temptation, a lie or a fear comes at us, we return to Christ. The whole armour does not make me stronger; it hides me more deeply in the Lord.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Scripture is my standard: the sword of the Spirit is the word of God. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he teaches me when to raise the shield. Jesus is my example: he overcame in the wilderness with “It is written.” These three foundations are our armour for every day.
q: Who is God? — God himself supplies the whole armour. What kind of Commander does this show you?
Who am I? — Which piece of armour do you most often forget to put on?
How shall I respond? — Which verse will you memorise today to be the sword in your hand?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, all three of his answers began, “It is written.” He did not prove himself with a miracle, and he did not debate with the devil; he simply stood firm on the word of God. He himself showed us how to take up the sword of the Spirit.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are my truth, my righteousness, my peace and my salvation. Today I put you on, and I take up the shield of faith and the word of God. Holy Spirit, remind me to stand in Christ whenever an attack comes. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: In the morning, take one minute to “put on” each piece of armour in prayer
Memorise a verse that confronts your greatest weakness
When temptation comes, say that verse, silently or aloud
lessons.noon: “And the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God” — Lord, right now I stand firm on your word.

lessons.title: Strong in the Lord
lessons.theme: The battle belongs to the Lord, not to me

v: and that all this assembly may know that the LORD doesn’t save with sword and spear; for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hand.”
He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.

lessons.still: Name a “giant” that frightens you: a difficulty, a weakness, a situation with no end in sight. Call it by name, then say, “Lord, you are bigger than this.” Quietly trust him.
teach: When the shepherd boy David was about to face the towering Goliath, Saul dressed him in his own armour. But David was not used to it and took it off, going out with only his staff, five smooth stones and his sling. He relied not on better equipment but on a deeper knowledge: this battle belonged to the Lord.

David said, “The battle is Yahweh’s.” Paul heard the Lord say, “My power is made perfect in weakness.” Both passages point to the same truth: strength is not puffing ourselves up but relying on the Lord’s mighty power. Paul even says, “When I am weak, then am I strong.” Admitting our weakness becomes the very doorway through which Christ’s power comes to rest on us.

This week’s memory verse says, “Be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of his might.” In spiritual warfare the most dangerous people are not the weak but those who think they are strong. They put on Saul’s armour and fight their own way. Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself. Relying on ourselves brings worry; relying on the Lord brings victory.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is laying down power and returning to our place. Admitting “I can’t” is our place as human beings; declaring “The Lord can” is letting God be God. The proud rely on their own armour; the humble rely on the name of the Lord. This is how humility overcomes pride and the self-emptied life overcomes Satan.
q: Who is God? — “My grace is sufficient for you.” Where have you recently experienced these words?
Who am I? — Are you still wearing “Saul’s armour,” fighting your own way?
How shall I respond? — Which weakness will you confess to the Lord today, so that his power may rest on you?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus looked weakest of all: nailed, mocked, forsaken. Yet it was there that he disarmed the principalities and powers and triumphed over them by the cross. God’s power was made perfect in the utter weakness of the cross.
lessons.pray: Lord, I admit that I am weak, and I admit that I often try to be strong in myself. Today I take off my own armour and rely on your name alone. Your grace is sufficient for me. Let your power be made perfect in my weakness, for the battle belongs to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down your current “giant,” and next to it write, “The battle is the Lord’s”
Confess one weakness to a spiritual companion and ask them to pray for you
Before each difficult task today, pray, “Lord, I rely on you.”
lessons.noon: “My grace is sufficient for you” — Lord, right now in my weakness I rely on your mighty power.

lessons.title: Prayer Is Warfare
lessons.theme: Prayer is an unseen battlefield, and a battlefield we share as a team

v: with all prayer and requests, praying at all times in the Spirit, and being watchful to this end in all perseverance and requests for all the saints.
When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.

lessons.still: Raise both hands for one minute and feel your arms slowly grow heavy. Think of Moses, and think of those who have prayed for you. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I need someone to hold up my hands, and I am willing to hold up the hands of others.”
teach: On a battlefield, the soldiers at the front can see the enemy; the signallers in the rear cannot. Yet if communications are cut, the front line is left stranded. Prayer is the communication line of spiritual warfare, linking the battlefield to the Commander. It looks unremarkable, yet victory or defeat depends on it.

Right after listing the whole armour, Ephesians says, “praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and requests.” Prayer is not just one more piece of equipment; it is how we wear the armour and go into battle. Exodus 17 makes it concrete: Joshua fought in the valley while Moses raised his hands on the hill. When Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed. When his hands grew heavy, Aaron and Hur held them up, one on each side, until sunset.

This is a picture of team prayer: some are on the front line, some are on the hill, and some hold up the hands of the one who prays. No one can keep their hands raised forever. This is what fellow soldiers are for: when the other person’s hands grow heavy, you hold them up, one on each side. Three weeks ago we learned about praying with one heart; today we see that praying with one heart is fighting with one heart.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The fellow soldiers in 235 do not only work together in ministry; they share the load in prayer. Prayer is an act of letting Jesus reign: it admits that victory is not in my hands but in God’s. To pray the Lord’s Prayer to its fulfilment is to give the kingdom, the power and the glory back to God.
q: Who is God? — Why did God link the victory to Moses’ raised hands in prayer?
Who am I? — Are you Moses raising his hands, Aaron and Hur holding them up, or someone who usually fights alone?
How shall I respond? — Whose hands among your fellow soldiers will you hold up this week?
lessons.jesus: In Gethsemane, in deep anguish, Jesus prayed all the more earnestly, and his sweat fell to the ground like great drops of blood. He took three disciples with him and asked them to keep watch and pray. The victory of the cross was first settled in prayer.
lessons.pray: Lord, teach me to treat prayer as warfare, not routine. Help me to pray at all times in the Spirit, with all kinds of prayers, and for all the saints. Give me a heart to support others, so that when a fellow soldier’s hands grow heavy, I will hold them up until victory comes. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Ask a fellow soldier, “What can I pray for you?”
Spend fifteen focused minutes praying for a co-worker serving on the front line
Set a reminder to pray for all the saints for one minute at the same time every day
lessons.noon: “Praying at all times in the Spirit” — Lord, right now I lift up my hands to you.

lessons.title: Standing Firm
lessons.theme: Resist the devil; overcome by the blood of the Lamb and our testimony

v: Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death.

lessons.still: Plant both feet flat on the floor and feel how solid the ground is beneath you. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I stand on your word and in your precious blood.” Take three deep breaths, and with each one declare in your heart, “I stand firm.”
teach: After a typhoon, the trees uprooted along the shore are often the ones with lush foliage but shallow roots. Old trees that have weathered many storms may be bent, but they have not fallen. Spiritual victory does not always mean routing the enemy; it means still “standing” in the storm.

Peter describes the devil as a roaring lion prowling around, looking for someone to devour, and lions go after the stragglers and the careless. The response is to be sober, to be watchful, to resist him firm in the faith, and to know that “your brothers in the world are undergoing the same sufferings”: you are not alone. Revelation 12:11 reveals the secret of victory: the blood of the Lamb, the word of our testimony, and not loving our lives.

This week we have seen the nature of the battle (Day 1), the whole armour (Day 2), being strong in the Lord (Day 3) and prayer as warfare (Day 4). Today it is standing firm. We stand not because we are strong but because the Lamb has already won. Next week we move to another front line, money, and ask who is reigning in our wallets.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life overcomes Satan, and “they didn’t love their life” is the self-emptied life at its fullest. Satan can accuse those who live a self-ruled life, but he cannot defeat someone who is wholly hidden in the blood of the Lamb and lives for the Lord. Our focus is not the lion’s roar but the Lamb who has already won.
q: Who is God? — The blood of the Lamb has already overcome the accuser. How does this change the way you see Satan’s attacks?
Who am I? — Are you currently isolated or careless?
How shall I respond? — With whom will you share a “word of your testimony”?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said to Peter, “But I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail.” He knew Peter would fall, yet he prayed for him beforehand and restored him after the resurrection. We can stand firm because our High Priest always lives to intercede for us.
lessons.pray: Victorious Lamb, I stand in your precious blood and will no longer be shaken by the voice of the accuser. Make me sober and watchful, resisting the devil firm in the faith. I do not cling to my own life; I only long for you to be glorified in me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down a testimony of God’s victory that you have personally experienced
Agree with a spiritual companion to check in on and watch over each other this week
Before sleep, declare, “I overcome by the blood of the Lamb.”
lessons.noon: “They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony” — Lord, right now I stand in your victory.
